Feature: Add race condition detection to Go tests

# GitHub Issue #145: Add race condition detection to Go tests with -race flag

**Category**: testing / reliability | **Scope**: Small

**Description**: Unit and integration tests currently run without the `-race` flag. Kubernetes operator code is inherently concurrent — reconcilers, watches, and informer caches all operate across goroutines. Race conditions are a frequent and hard-to-diagnose source of bugs in this type of codebase. A dedicated CI job should run all Go tests with `-race` enabled, and a corresponding Makefile target should be added for local use.

Makefile extension:

```makefile
test-race:
	cd internal/common && go test -race ./...
	cd operators/keystone && go test -race ./...
```

Proposed CI job (separate from the main test job since `-race` adds ~2-5x overhead):

```yaml
test-race:
  needs: [changes]
  if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  timeout-minutes: 20
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
      with:
        go-version-file: go.work
    - run: |
        cd internal/common && go test -race -count=1 ./...
        cd operators/keystone && go test -race -count=1 ./...
```

<subject-line>
  <rule name="format">"plan(CC-0052): <short description>"</rule>
  <rule name="types">feat | fix | test | refactor | docs | style | chore</rule>
  <rule name="length">Max 50 chars recommended, 72 chars absolute maximum</rule>
  <rule name="style">Imperative mood ("add" not "added", "fix" not "fixed")</rule>
  <rule name="punctuation">No period at end, capitalize after colon</rule>
</subject-line>

<body optional="true">
  <rule>Blank line required between subject and body</rule>
  <rule>Wrap lines at 72 characters maximum</rule>
  <rule>Explain WHAT changed and WHY (not HOW)</rule>
</body>

<avoid>
  <rule>Include "WIP", "temp", "test", or placeholder text</rule>
  <rule>Commit unrelated changes in the same commit</rule>
  <rule>Use past tense ("added", "fixed", "changed")</rule>
  <rule>Include issue numbers without context</rule>
</avoid>

<never-stage>
  NEVER stage or commit build/runtime artifacts. Before running `git add`,
  verify that NONE of these are included:
  - Python: __pycache__/, *.pyc, *.pyo, .venv/, venv/, .mypy_cache/,
    .ruff_cache/, .pytest_cache/, *.egg-info/, dist/, build/, .tox/, .nox/
  - Node.js: node_modules/, .next/, .turbo/, .parcel-cache/
  - Rust: target/, *.rlib
  - Go: *.test binary outputs
  - Compiled: *.exe, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib, *.o, *.obj, *.a, *.wasm
  - JVM: *.class, *.jar, *.war, *.ear
  - .NET: bin/, obj/, *.nupkg
  - Terraform: .terraform/, *.tfstate
  - OS: .DS_Store, Thumbs.db
  Use `git add <specific-files>` instead of `git add .` or `git add -A`.
  If in doubt, run `git status` first and only stage source files.
</never-stage>
</commit-best-practices>
